I found no literature to draw on, so these hypotheses rest on prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201. Convolutions are strong, skip_connect is moderate, avg_pool_3x3 is weak and none is weakest. They fall into three groups:

- **Replacing the parent value on the same edge.** Filling a "none" slot with a convolution helps more than replacing another op. Swapping a strong op for a weak one hurts more than swapping a weak one.
- **Disconnecting a conv edit.** Setting another edge to none cuts the edited edge off from the output. The usual positive effect of a conv edit then falls toward zero, so it is lower.
- **Disconnecting a removal edit.** Edits to none usually hurt. When the edge is already disconnected, the effect moves toward zero, so it is higher.
